protein aggregation is not only a consequence of a protein being intrinsically disordered, but it is also a consequence of a globular protein losing its ability to interact with its binding partner.

The main takeaway from our work is that

protein-protein interaction surfaces and aggregation prone regions frequently overlap, which suggests that protein complexes and their individual subunits may compete in the cell for binding partners and for the formation of toxic assemblies.
the formation of protein complexes and aggregation of globular polypeptides are not mutually exclusive processes.
protein aggregation underlies a broad range of human disorders, but the molecular basis of this pathological process is not the same for all proteins.
